key_insight: The paper introduces an ontology-grounded benchmark pipeline that generates multiple-choice questions with correct and incorrect answers that are formally verified against OWL ontologies.
engineering_relevance: This gives materials and scientific AI teams a reliable way to test whether LLMs can reason correctly over structured domain knowledge instead of only matching surface patterns.
method: Start from a sufficiently axiomatised OWL 2 ontology and derive MCQs from class definition axioms.
Generate distractors by perturbing right-hand-side class expressions.
Use a reasoner to verify that distractors are truly incorrect via entailment checks.
evidence_signal: Across Pizza, PMDco, and DOID the pipeline produced 112, 2,491, and 15,216 MCQs, and zero-shot LLM accuracy ranged from 41.1% to 76.8% versus a 25% random baseline.
watch_item: Benchmark quality depends on the ontology being sufficiently axiomatised, so sparse or inconsistent source ontologies may limit coverage and validity.
paper_title: Ontology-Grounded, Reasoner-Verified Benchmarks for Evaluating LLM Reasoning in Scientific AI
